_note: Sixty goods clear through world markets at prices the register clamps at seventy-five per cent either way, and the occasions here are the mornings the bill arrives. Nothing in this file causes a shortage -- the register carries flows, not stocks -- these are the politics of one that already happened at the wharf. The last two events, com_price_high_desk and com_industry_bills, are ordinary hazard events at the median likelihood of the six above (0.0033). They were authored as commodity_price_high hook events (0.45 and 0.40 per happening) and UNBOUND at pass 23: the V4.6 price drift crosses goods one after another in months 1-5 of every new game for all 29 nations and never again, so the hook fired only inside that artefact. commodity_price_high stays in the vocabulary with no consumer, like law_passed; re-bind them once the drift is fixed. Their prose names no good and ties to no happening: whichever import is running high, the card has to be true of it.

events.name: The winter bill
events.summary: Wholesale gas is at the price the utilities warn about in papers nobody reads, storage is exactly where the operators said it would be, and the bill is still landing on every doorstep by February. The tariff is the policy now, whoever it belongs to.
events.speaker_line: Wholesale price did what we warned, storage behaved, and now every household will see it on paper by February unless you choose.

choices.label: Freeze the household tariff
choices.summary: The utility eats the spread and the state lends it the difference at a rate the next government inherits. The pensioners' bills hold and the debt office adds a line it did not have.

choices.label: Let the tariff move
choices.summary: The price does what prices do and the state sends pensioners a cheque in March, when the coldest bills are already paid. The market calls it discipline and the kitchen tables call it February.

choices.label: Ask the utilities to be understanding
choices.summary: They are understanding for one quarter, with interest. The bill arrives whole in April, with the operator's apology attached.

events.name: The harvest that failed over there
events.summary: The bread wheat failed two markets away -- weather, then logistics, then export bans, in the order they always arrive. The millers have covered a quarter of the gap and the bakers have done their own arithmetic about March.
events.speaker_line: My mills cannot carry this price into spring, and I would rather argue for help now than explain closed bakeries later.

choices.label: Carry the millers' bill
choices.summary: The state stands between the world price and the flour price for the season, and the co-ops plant on the strength of it. The treasury owns a subsidy with a harvest's name on it, which is a habit that outlives harvests.

choices.label: Pay the world price and pass it on
choices.summary: Flour costs what flour costs and the baker's sign explains it daily. The farm gate does well out of somebody else's drought, which the town reads as a tax with wheat on it.

choices.label: Wait for the southern harvest
choices.summary: It is eleven weeks out and the bakers' arithmetic says four. The price does the talking until then, and it is not using words.

events.name: The minerals letter
events.summary: The producer of most of the world's battery minerals has moved two of them to a licence list in the same week, and the plant the car factories answer to has nine weeks of the old price left. The letter calls it industrial policy; the order books call it what it is.
events.speaker_line: Two minerals moved to licence list this week, our plant holds nine weeks of old price, and a letter will not feed an order book.

choices.label: Pool the orders with the other buyers
choices.summary: Six buyers signing one contract is a monopsony until the producer reads it as one, which they do within the month. The price softens by a fifth and the relationship learns that it is a hostage too.

choices.label: Underwrite the plant's input bill
choices.summary: The difference between the contract price and the spot price is paid from the infrastructure line for as long as the letter says. The factories keep their shifts and the ministry keeps a chart of what loyalty costs.

choices.label: Let the contracts reprice
choices.summary: The spot market reprices and the car factories reprice with it, quarterly. The mines are no closer and the transition plan loses a season it does not get back.

events.name: The spread that did not
events.summary: The fertiliser plant is down for want of the gas it runs on, the import order is queued behind two bigger ones, and the co-op says the dressing window is six weeks. The farms will carry whatever the government decides; the question is whether the town shares it.
events.speaker_line: Fertiliser plant sits idle for want of gas, our import sits in a queue, and the co-op says six weeks is all the dressing window allows.

choices.label: Buy the cargo out of turn
choices.summary: A season's dressing at this spring's price, paid against the farm credit line the state stands behind. The co-op plants on time and the treasury owns a hedging story it will still be telling in five years.

choices.label: Ration by holding
choices.summary: The co-op allocates by holding size, which the big farms call collectivism and the small ones call the first fair spring in years. The yields carry the argument in September, one way or the other.

choices.label: Let the market do the rationing
choices.summary: It does, by price. The dressing goes to whoever can carry a spring on margins, and the smallholdings go to whoever can carry an autumn.

events.name: The strait
events.summary: The lane that carries a third of the country's crude has closed for an inspection season nobody had scheduled, and the tankers are queueing at the anchorage in two directions. The strategic reserve is a flow and not a tank, which the operator now explains with a chart.
events.speaker_line: The lane carrying a third of our crude has closed, tankers queue both ways, and I now have a chart explaining why reserve is flow not tank.

choices.label: Pay the long way round
choices.summary: Fourteen extra days at sea on every barrel, on the freight bill the refineries pass through by August. The pumps hold, the hauliers hold, and the fare is in everything that moves.

choices.label: Open the strategic terminals to the spot market
choices.summary: The berths the navy keeps for the navy open to whoever pays the dues. The queue shortens by the weekend and the base commander's letter arrives after the decision, as letters do.

choices.label: Let the queue clear
choices.summary: Inspection seasons end. The price peaks where the queues are longest and the blame settles where the terminals are, which is here.

events.name: The mine that stopped
events.summary: The copper belt's oldest mine has been out three weeks and the smelters on this side of the trade are running on named tonnes and good manners. Wire is a quarter of everything the grid builds, a figure the grid operator now mentions in every schedule.
events.speaker_line: My smelters cannot keep running on goodwill, so I need to hear how the state plans to bring both sides back to talking.

choices.label: Buy the year forward
choices.summary: A year of wire at a price that hurts once instead of monthly. The smelters keep their bookings and the treasury keeps a contract it will be congratulated for and never thanked for.

choices.label: Stretch the grid programme
choices.summary: The interconnect slips a year and the build season absorbs what the mine does not deliver. The commissioning dates move in one paragraph and are noticed by nobody but the contractors, who bid accordingly.

choices.label: Bid at the spot and complain
choices.summary: Everyone bids, the price answers, and the programme pays it because stopping is dearer. The strike fund in the producer country receives, in effect, a small levy on your electricity meter.

events.name: The price is the policy now
events.summary: World prices for something the country's industry depends on are running well above the level budgets were set against, and the question on the desk is the one every government answers badly: absorb it, pass it through, or find somebody to blame. The world price does not care which. The kitchen tables keep a record.
events.speaker_line: My firm will not absorb this squeeze for long, and I need to know before the next order whether the state intends to stand with us.

choices.label: Absorb it in the budget
choices.summary: The infrastructure line is raised to pay the spread, and the world price is left to remember its manners in its own time. The bills hold, the debt holds the difference, and nobody thanks a subsidy for not happening.

choices.label: Let it pass through
choices.summary: The price reaches the shelf in one hop, which is at least honest. The exporters and the farms like the world as it is; the pensioners price it weekly.

choices.label: Announce an inquiry into the margins
choices.summary: There is always a middleman and one of them is in your coalition. The inquiry reports after the price has settled, into margins that have moved on.

events.name: The factories' input bill
events.summary: World prices have been running at a level the federation's arithmetic cannot live with, and it has arrived with the sums: the mills are buying at margins that close in eight weeks. It would like the state to decide who eats the difference, the market having declined to.
events.speaker_line: Our members are not asking for charity, only a decision about who pays, because silence will settle it by closing the weakest mills first.

choices.label: Take the mills in hand
choices.summary: The state takes the input allocation for industry into its own hands, with a rulebook attached, and the rulebook is a standing load on the sector. The mill workers like the attention; the owners, who have to file for it, and the farms, who are asked to wait, do not.

choices.label: Free the import channel
choices.summary: The duties on the inputs come off and the customs line gives up the revenue, which was the point. The mills buy at the world price and the farms meet the world's mills.

choices.label: Let the margins close
choices.summary: The weak close, the strong buy their orders back cheaper in the spring, and the federation's next visit is about the closures. The region reads it in the wage figures first.
